strengths: Manners/operator request vs statute is the correct split (watch item).
Priority-seat policy change over time is not frozen as 2010 blog advice.
Shinkansen deck / phone corner treated as a wrinkle, not a universal car type.
verified: Voice calls on trains are generally not a criminal prohibition.
Many operators announce silent mode and refrain from talking on phones.
Silent phone use (text, maps, games) is ordinary.
questionable: ‘Drivers and conductors make their own calls for operations’: operations use radios/PA; ‘calls’ can be misread as passenger-style phone chat from staff.
needs_source: Do not cite a specific operator’s current priority-seat electromagnetic rule as nationwide without the sticker.

issues.location: Texting Is Fine — drivers and conductors
issues.problem: Operational radio/PA is not the same as a phone call; the uniform-vs-passenger distinction still stands.
issues.suggestion: ‘Staff announcements and radios are work noise; a passenger meeting is not.’

issues.location: Announcements — ‘You are unlikely to be arrested’
issues.problem: True in the trivial sense; frames manners as if criminal law were the alternative.
issues.suggestion: Unlikely to be ticketed or removed for a short call; you have still broken the local deal.
